answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a cooling-off period before it may vote or earn reputation. One attacker can create an echo of accounts, but each must tie up real capital, and reclaiming it takes time; splitting influence into a spiral of identities therefore multiplies the deposit and opportunity cost rather than creating free weight. The zenith of the attack is bounded by how much capital the attacker can afford to immobilize.
